title: Environment Promotion Enterprise Standard
description: Canonical USF-193 environment promotion and readiness gate definition for dev, test, staging, and production. This is a semantic gate and enterprise evidence organisation artefact only; it does not claim readiness for any environment.
aiGuidance: Do not infer readiness across environments. Provider mode, environment, proof level, freshness, and approval remain separate dimensions. This standard defines gates; it does not satisfy them.

environmentStandards.purpose: Fast local development and bounded proof using in-memory or hermetic providers by default, with Compose only where a specific proof boundary requires a real local service.
proofRequirements: Provider mode is reported explicitly as hermetic-mock unless a specific Compose-backed proof declares local-composed-real-service.
Synthetic tenant, actor, and job data only.
Tenant mismatch and authorization failure paths fail closed.
Audit evidence is value-free and commit-linked.
No lower or higher environment readiness claim is emitted.
enterpriseEvidenceRequirements: owner, risk owner, control owner, and evidence owner recorded
tenant boundary and access boundary recorded
promotionPrerequisites: Any Compose-backed dev proof declares local-composed-real-service and service-catalogue linkage
environmentStandards.requiredApprover: USF-192 coordinator for later readiness assessment

riskTreatment.riskStatement: Dev proof could be overclaimed as test, staging, production, live-provider, full-dev, or full-parity readiness.
riskTreatment.threatFailureScenario: A passing in-memory or bounded local proof is treated as a stronger environment readiness claim.
riskTreatment.treatment: mitigate through validator-enforced provider and environment separation plus explicit non-claims

environmentStandards.purpose: Fully composed local test substrate for required services and providers, with destructive reset and exhaustive synthetic-data testing where applicable.
proofRequirements: Every required service/provider is composed or explicitly deferred by a linked source issue.
No in-memory provider satisfies test-composed proof.
Reset, migration, rollback, purge, provider-failure, and tenant-isolation failure testing is allowed only against disposable synthetic data.
Provider and service proof outputs are command-pinned and current for the assessed commit.
No staging, production, live-provider, SOC, ISO, deployment, full-dev, full-parity, or USF-133 closure claim is emitted.
enterpriseEvidenceRequirements: service catalogue linkage for every required service
provider-mode evidence for every adapter proof
promotionPrerequisites: USF-167 compose service disposition gate merged and reconciled
All required service rows closed, deferred with owner and follow-up, or explicitly out of scope
Compose and runtime validators pass on the current commit
Enterprise evidence rows record unresolved promotion impact
environmentStandards.requiredApprover: USF-192 coordinator plus source issue owners

riskTreatment.riskStatement: In-memory proof or partially composed proof could be treated as complete test readiness.
riskTreatment.threatFailureScenario: A required composed service/provider is silently omitted while test readiness is implied.
riskTreatment.treatment: mitigate with service-disposition and provider-proof validators; defer unresolved rows to linked source issues

environmentStandards.purpose: Production-shaped release and migration rehearsal using controlled non-production data and non-destructive operational posture.
proofRequirements: Migration rehearsal and rollback rehearsal are current and non-destructive.
Config, secret, observability, alert-routing, compatibility, and release-promotion evidence exists.
Representative data is controlled non-production data unless a future explicit exception is approved.
Staging evidence cannot satisfy production-live readiness.
No production, live-provider, SOC, ISO, deployment, enterprise production, full-dev, full-parity, or USF-133 closure claim is emitted.
promotionPrerequisites: Test readiness assessment exists with current merged evidence
Production-shaped rehearsal evidence exists for the assessed commit
No destructive test semantics are used as staging evidence
Staging exceptions have owner, compensating control, expiry, validation command, and follow-up issue

riskTreatment.riskStatement: Staging rehearsal could be overclaimed as production-live readiness or use destructive test semantics against non-disposable data.
riskTreatment.threatFailureScenario: A production-shaped rehearsal hides missing release, migration, rollback, alerting, privacy, or incident evidence.
riskTreatment.treatment: defer staging readiness until a separate source issue proves non-destructive production-shaped rehearsal evidence

environmentStandards.purpose: Live tenant operation with authorised providers, governed access, operational controls, data protection, incident response, backup/restore, supplier posture, privacy controls, and approved residual risk.
proofRequirements: Production-live provider authority exists for every live provider.
Real secrets, access controls, monitoring, incident response, backup/restore, privacy controls, supplier posture, and approved residual risk are current.
Only non-destructive live smoke or health proof is permitted unless a future explicit exception is approved.
Production readiness is never inferred from dev, test, or staging evidence.
No SOC, ISO certification, enterprise production, full-dev, full-parity, or USF-133 closure claim is emitted by this standard.
enterpriseEvidenceRequirements: privacy, retention, purge, legal hold, data residency, and supplier evidence
promotionPrerequisites: Staging readiness assessment exists with current merged evidence
Live provider authority and supplier/subprocessor posture are approved
Production residual risk is approved by the risk owner
Operational evidence package is current and non-destructive
Release approval is recorded by the production approver

riskTreatment.riskStatement: Production readiness could be inferred from lower-environment proof or incomplete operational controls.
riskTreatment.threatFailureScenario: Live operation begins without provider authority, approved residual risk, incident response, backup/restore, privacy, access review, or release approval evidence.
riskTreatment.treatment: defer production readiness until separate production source issues and approvals provide current merged evidence

requiredEvidence: USF-167 service disposition gate for required composed services
current runtime and provider proof where provider ports exist
enterprise evidence rows for owners, data boundary, tenant boundary, access boundary, and non-claims
forbiddenEvidenceSubstitutions: in-memory provider proof cannot satisfy test composed proof
dev smoke proof cannot satisfy test readiness
generated reports cannot replace proof evidence

requiredEvidence: non-destructive production-shaped migration and release rehearsal plan
observability, alerting, incident, privacy, security scanning, and rollback evidence
forbiddenEvidenceSubstitutions: destructive test reset cannot satisfy staging data posture
test composed proof cannot satisfy staging rehearsal
local Compose topology cannot imply external sandbox or production-shaped readiness

requiredEvidence: live provider authority and supplier/subprocessor approvals
production operational controls, access review, incident response, backup/restore, privacy, release approval, and approved residual risk
forbiddenEvidenceSubstitutions: staging rehearsal cannot satisfy production-live readiness
external sandbox proof cannot satisfy live-external-provider readiness
production-shaped topology cannot satisfy production-live evidence

claimRules: dev evidence must not satisfy test readiness
test evidence must not satisfy staging readiness
staging evidence must not satisfy production readiness
production readiness requires explicit production-live evidence and approval
hermetic-mock provider mode must not satisfy local-composed-real-service, external-sandbox, or live-external-provider requirements
destructive test semantics must not satisfy staging or production posture
readiness claims must not exceed proof level, provider mode, environment class, freshness, and approval evidence
ISO/SOC/certification, enterprise production, full dev, full React parity, and USF-133 closure claims remain prohibited
enterpriseAssuranceRequirements: owner, risk owner, control owner, and evidence owner
identity, SSO/OIDC, MFA, RBAC/ABAC, SCIM/user lifecycle where applicable
admin/operator access, break-glass, JIT access, access review, and deprovisioning
data classification, PII, retention, purge, legal hold, export, privacy/DSR, and data residency
secrets, KMS/key ownership, rotation, TLS/cert lifecycle, and no secret logging
structured logs, metrics, traces, correlation IDs, tenant-safe labels, redaction, and audit events
alerting, dashboards, incident response, escalation, post-incident review, and evidence preservation
SAST, dependency scanning, secret scanning, container/image scanning, SBOM, license posture, SDK governance, vulnerability exception, and patch SLA
application security verification posture for auth, session, access control, input/API/file/upload/error/security-header/rate-limit controls
backup/restore, RPO/RTO, failover, timeout/retry, circuit breakers, queue drain, worker replay, migration rollback, and provider outage scenarios
change approval, release evidence pack, migration plan, rollback plan, feature flags, phased rollout, compatibility, API deprecation, and customer-impact assessment

customer-facing enterprise feature posture including audit export, SSO/SAML/OIDC, SCIM, role templates, custom retention, data export/delete, support access approval, customer-managed keys, data residency, IP allowlisting, private networking, webhook signing, and admin reporting

prohibitedInferences: in-memory provider proof implies composed service proof
enterprise evidence organisation implies ISO/SOC certification
falseClosureGuards: validation passing alone is not Done
wrapper issue completion is not source issue completion
USF-133 remains open until every parent acceptance criterion is individually satisfied
USF-167 remains a separate service-disposition execution gate
